subject.title: fix: require decimal numeric oc-path predicates

question: Should relational oc-path predicates preserve the existing finite-number contract, including exponent-form values, while rejecting coercion artifacts, or should OpenClaw intentionally adopt a plain-decimal-only predicate grammar?
rationale: The patch makes a compatibility-sensitive language change, and neither the PR body nor the supplied discussion establishes that narrowing exponent-form input is an approved product contract.

options.title: Preserve finite-number compatibility
options.body: Reject blank-string and unintended coercions but retain finite formats that the established predicate contract supports, including exponent notation if documented.

options.title: Adopt plain-decimal-only predicates
options.body: Accept the new grammar as intentional, then update the public contract and provide upgrade-facing proof that existing predicate usage will not be surprised.

recommendation.title: Preserve finite-number compatibility
recommendation.body: Reject blank-string and unintended coercions but retain finite formats that the established predicate contract supports, including exponent notation if documented.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline provides the only concrete maintainer-side discussion signal for this PR.
